transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: Thu Feb 5 2026 15:00 PST
Duration: 47 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (Sapphire ML Eng), Maria (Product), Devon (Infra), Samir (CTO)

Summary: quick pass on latest pilot numbers — tokens/sec per dollar, caching savings, and batching tradeoffs. Goal: pick production knobs for next 2-week pilot and lock infra window for side-by-side runs.

Topics:
- Current baseline performance (hosted)
- Caching (prefix/KV) measured impact
- Batching size vs p50/p95/p99 latency
- Dedicated vs Hosted economics for steady 5k reqs/day
- Security/VPC peering questions

Action items (from transcript): see action_items metadata above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: all right uh hey everyone thanks for joining, quick note on agenda, we'll start w numbers then go into tuning recommendations, um Priya over to you for the runbook highlights?
[00:18] Priya: yep thanks Jordan. so we re-ran the throughput sweep overnight with the updated quant profile — q4_8bit — and we saw tokens per second per dollar improvement from about 12 tok/sec/$ to 18 tok/sec/$ on average with batching enabled. that's with hosted nodes and the default cache settings.
[00:41] Alex: sorry can you repeat the baseline, 12 tok — was that with no caching?
[00:46] Priya: yeah baseline no prefix cache, batch size 1. when we enable prefix/KV caching we saw a further uplift; effective tokens/sec/$ hit ~24 in a steady-state read-heavy workload. caveat: that was on the synthetic prompt set — real prompt variety is lower cache hit, closer to 20.
[01:10] Maria: so around 20 tok/sec/$ realistic for our usage? that would be great, how much does that change latency?
[01:18] Priya: good q. small batch sizes (1-4) keep p50 sub-120ms, p95 about 280ms. if we push batch to 8 or 16, tokens/sec/$ goes up ~10-25% depending on model, but p99 jumps by 60-120ms. p50 stays similar. we measured batch=8 gives ~27 tok/sec/$ but p99 around 420ms in our tests.
[01:46] Devon: 420ms p99 is kinda high for interactive product; our UX target is 300ms p99 ideally.
[01:53] Priya: understood. there's room for hybrid — route latency-sensitive routes through smaller batch / reserved fast path and background or low-priority through larger batch. Redwood routing policies can do that.
[02:08] Samir: also curious on caching savings — you said uplift, can you talk % savings on token spending?
[02:14] Priya: yes, measured token spend reduction about 22-35% depending on prompt overlap. prefix cache saved ~35% of repeated prefix tokens on the synthetic prompts. with real traffic we saw ~22% savings in app telemetry sample.
[02:30] Alex: is that KV cache or prefix only? we use a few long docs and a lot of short queries.
[02:35] Priya: primarily prefix/KV combined; KV for big doc embeddings/lookup, prefix for repeated system prompts and user conversation history. sometimes transcription picked up K-V as K-V cash (laugh).
[02:47] Jordan: ha, yeah that transcription issue again. ok. next, economics: if you move to Dedicated 3-node pool (reserved), our estimate for your workload (5k req/day, avg 120 tokens out) shows cost per token down ~12-18% vs hosted pay-as-you-go, plus predictable latency. but commit cost upfront.
[03:12] Maria: numbers please, are we talking monthly difference?
[03:16] Jordan: yes — rough: hosted estimated $Xk/month (~$12k) vs Dedicated reserved ~ $10.2k/month equivalent after commit discounts; I'll send the full quote.
[03:28] Devon: and Dedicated supports private VPC peering, right? for data residency?
[03:32] Priya: yes, Dedicated can be in your VPC or peered — and for Private on-prem we have the package too but that adds infra ops cost. Dedicated gets KMS integration and audit logs, SOC2 standard.
[03:46] Alex: is there any difference in quantization support between Hosted and Dedicated?
[03:50] Priya: no functional difference — runtime kernels selected per node orientation. Dedicated gives more control on kernel/quant profiles; we can pin to q4_8bit or try Q5_6bit for your hallucination profile tests. Q5 might save a few % more cost but could slightly change output distribution.
[04:10] Samir: risk profile on hallucinations is important for us; product can't tolerate more than tiny uptick.
[04:15] Priya: understood — we'll run a qa pass on the prompt set and track regression metrics. Redwood Optimize can surface quality regressions vs baseline.
[04:24] Jordan: ok let's surface the p95/p99 tradeoff again. Alex, what are the high-priority routes?
[04:29] Alex: routing is about 3 routes: 1) conversational chat (high latency sensitivity), 2) document summarization (batch-friendly), 3) re-ranking pipeline (throughput critical).
[04:40] Priya: recommended: route 1 to hosted or dedicated fast-pool with batch size 1-2 and prefix cache; route 2 to batched pool with batches 8-16 and aggressive prefix+KV; route 3 we can use dedicated throughput-optimized nodes with larger batch & KV cache and also async job style.
[04:58] Maria: what about tokenization differences? our first pass tokenization had more tokens than expected.
[05:03] Priya: we saw your corpus tokenization ~1.18x of baseline for same content, mostly due to extra system prompt framing. simple win: reduce system prompt verbosity and move static context to KV cache so it's not re-sent per request. that shaved ~8% tokens in test.
[05:20] Devon: network egress — if we peer VPC, are there extra charges in your quote?
[05:25] Jordan: some cloud egress still applies depending on region and peering mode; we'll annotate quote with expected egress assumptions.
[05:32] Alex: competitor question — if we ran against MegaAI for throughput, what would be different?
[05:36] Priya: in our side-by-sides we usually see competing managed vendors trade off caching support and kernel optimizations. MegaAI in our last 3 tests lagged in prefix cache policy flexibility and had less transparent latency breakdowns; but every test's details vary. we'll set up a direct run if you want.
[05:54] Jordan: ok let's talk immediate next steps — Priya, you'll run the 48h sweep with the three batch configs, prefix cache on/off, and produce CSV w p50/p95/p99 and tok/sec/$ column. include both hosted and Dedicated-simulated numbers.
[06:08] Priya: yes, I'll include both and flag routes that violate the 300ms p99 target.
[06:12] Alex: good. also can we see per-route TTL recommendations for cache?
[06:16] Priya: yes — recommend shorter TTL for chat ephemeral context (30-60s), longer for doc chunks (6-24h) depending on mutability. I'll add TTL column in the CSV.
[06:27] Maria: and on the security ask — we need SOC2 and encryption at rest details.
[06:31] Jordan: will include SOC2 attestation, KMS integration doc, and audit log sample.
[06:35] Devon: we'll need a maintenance window for VPC peering — tentatively next Tue 02/10 02:00-04:00 UTC.
[06:42] Jordan: noted, we'll schedule with infra team.
[06:45] Samir: any red flags? performance regressions?
[06:48] Priya: none significant; one gotcha was tokenization inflation from your prompt wrapper — easily fixed. also watch the p99 with big batch sizes.
[06:58] Alex: can we also get a simple dashboard view of tokens/sec/$ and cache hit over time?
[07:03] Jordan: Redwood Console can surface that; I'll request a demo dashboard link and a short screencap.
[07:10] Priya: one more note — if you elect Dedicated, autoscaling policy can still burst to hosted capacity for spikes; that's a hybrid you might like. it preserves baseline latency while not overcommitting.
[07:23] Maria: hmm that sounds useful for Black Friday style spikes, thanks.
[07:27] Jordan: ok wrapping — recap of next steps and dates. any final q's?
[07:31] Alex: none from me. thanks everyone.
[07:35] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up with quote, CSV, and peering confirmation.

End of transcript.
